standard_prerequisites.name: The construction of the limit of a diagram of topological spaces over a cofiltered category, as the subset of the product with the induced topology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Given in the author's section on limits of spaces, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the limit and its projection maps in terms of which both assertions are formulated.

core_obligations: The basis of the product: the proof starts from the standard basis of the product topology consisting of products of opens that are the whole factor for almost all indices, and notes that only finitely many factors can be proper (proof lines 2604-2608).

Assertion (1): intersecting such a basis element with the limit gives a finite intersection of preimages of opens, which the author rewrites as the preimage of an open under the projection to a suitable index, giving the description of an arbitrary open of the limit (proof lines 2609-2625).

Assertion (2): for a quasi-compact open the author uses the finite description obtained in (1) together with quasi-compactness to reduce the finite union to a single projection-preimage, which is the content of the second assertion (proof lines 2625-2641).
Conclusion: any open of the limit is a union of projection-preimages, and any quasi-compact open is a single projection-preimage (proof lines 2641-2642).
proof_roadmap: 从乘积拓扑的标准基出发：只有有限多个因子上的开集是真子集，与极限相交后写成有限多个投影原像的交。
第 (1) 条把有限交整理成某个投影下的原像；第 (2) 条再利用紧性把有限并压成单个投影原像。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the description of the topology of a cofiltered limit of spaces (author lemma at source lines 2590-2601, label lemma-describe-limits): every open of the limit is a union of projection-preimages of opens, and every quasi-compact open is a single projection-preimage. The proof (source lines 2603-2642) computes with the standard basis of the product topology: it observes that only finitely many factors of a basis element can be proper, writes the intersection with the limit as a finite intersection of projection-preimages, and then uses quasi-compactness to collapse the finite union in the second assertion (proof lines 2604-2641). The distinction between arbitrary and quasi-compact opens is the point of the lemma and is what the later results on limits of spectral spaces use. H2.
